rationale: Table-heavy papers produce many similar table-row candidates and downstream multi-process assignment ambiguity. Instead of exploding candidate counts (per-cell) or adding paper-specific rules, include a compact, deterministic table fingerprint (hash of label+caption+headers) on each table-row candidate and add it to the candidate context and as a dedicated field. This preserves deterministic behavior, does not invent any domain-specific values, and gives downstream components a stable table-level key they can use for disambiguation or grouping without increasing candidate cardinality.

summary: Add deterministic table fingerprint to table-row inventory candidates to provide compact table-level disambiguating context

rationale: Table-heavy papers often produce many duplicate or near-identical table-row candidates that increase ambiguity and multi-process assignment counts. Without changing evidence thresholds or adding paper-specific logic, collapse identical table-row evidence within the same table into a single deterministic candidate that records all row indices in its source_location and context. This preserves all evidence (no invented values), is deterministic, keeps IDs stable, and reduces candidate cardinality so downstream assignment has less spurious ambiguity. Added a focused unit test demonstrating deduplication. No benchmark-specific logic or weakened checks were introduced.
regression_reasons: ambiguity increased or flow count fell
summary: Deterministic deduplication of identical table-row inventory candidates per table to reduce candidate explosion in table-heavy papers

rationale: Table-heavy papers often use <td> for header rows, leaving the parser without header context and increasing downstream ambiguity. Add a small deterministic heuristic: if no explicit <th> header rows are found and the first row appears non-numeric and alphabetic, treat it as a header row. This preserves determinism, adds no paper-specific rules or invented data, and gives downstream components more structured context to disambiguate similar table-row candidates. Added a unit test to assert header detection when headers are encoded with <td>.
regression_reasons: ambiguity increased or flow count fell
summary: Heuristic header detection for tables lacking <th> and test coverage

rationale: Table-heavy papers produce many similar table-row candidates which increase downstream assignment ambiguity. Add a small, deterministic, and general attribute to each InventoryCandidate: a numeric_signature that captures the sequence of numeric value + unit tokens found in the evidence text (e.g. '4.2 kg', '2.5 kwh'). This reuses existing extracted evidence, does not invent values or modify thresholds, is deterministic, and provides a compact machine-readable signal downstream can use to group or disambiguate candidates. Tests verify presence and content of the numeric_signature for table and section-derived candidates.

summary: Add deterministic numeric_signature to inventory candidates to give downstream disambiguation signal without changing extraction counts or thresholds

rationale: TABLE_HEAVY_UNRESOLVED arises from many similar table-row candidates causing downstream tie/ambiguity. Prior attempts that changed candidate cardinality or added table-specific fingerprints/regrouping regressed. This does not invent data, change thresholds, or alter candidate counts; it only augments candidates with a stable, lightweight signal downstream components can use for deterministic tie-breaking or ranking. Tests assert the new field exists and is well-formed.
